subject: Warning message some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others

messages.author: d8e75f3443fb0f5e
messages.subject: Warning message some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others
parts:
Hello 

I am new to SEM and lavaan package, forgive me if my question is too basic or not be described in an appropriate way.
I kept received a warning message after I fit my model. 
model<-
  '#measurement model
  Health_conditioning =~ TotalNumofMedicalConditions
  Physical_Functioning =~ Phy_HandStrength_avg + Phy_rawWalkTime
  Visual_Functioning =~ Vis_dyNrActyBoth_logMAR + Vis_periphRt_coded1 + Vis_VMIImpairmentLevel_coded + Vis_depthPercep
  Cognitive_Functioning =~ Con_ClockDrawingScore + Con_VisualSearchImpairmentLevel_coded + Con_UFOVImpairmentLevel_coded
    '
```{r}
fit <- cfa(model = model, data = data, ordered = c("Vis_periphRt_coded1", "Vis_VMIImpairmentLevel_coded", "Vis_depthPercep", "Con_ClockDrawingScore", "Con_VisualSearchImpairmentLevel_coded", "Con_UFOVImpairmentLevel_coded"))
```
Warning message: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate lavaan WARNING some observed variances are larger than 1000000.

Among all observed variables, Phy_HandStrength_avg  and Phy_rawWalkTime are continuous variables with mean 58.305 and 6002.172. Others are all ordered variables with less than 10 levels (1,2,3,4....). Is this cause of the warning message? Are there recommended procedure or tests  to fix it?

Thanks

messages.author: 6f81c58ba9ed02c3
messages.subject: Re: Warning message some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others
parts:
Hi Daniela,

Yes, those are the culprits. You can rescale them by dividing by a factor of 10. If memory serves correctly, if you were to divide the raw scores for those variables by 10, you would be reducing their variance by 100. This is a warning message and not an error message, so it could be that the difference in variance is not adversely affecting model estimation, but since it is pretty easy to rescale the variables, it doesn't hurt to do that and then run the model again.

Best,

Ryan
